name: LiteLLM
license: MIT, except content under the enterprise/ directory which is separately licensed
supported_backends: none (proxy layer - no local compute backend of its own)
supported_formats: passthrough (speaks OpenAI, Anthropic, Bedrock, Vertex, Azure, and native provider formats; model formats are irrelevant because it is not loading weights)
notable_features: A gateway/proxy, not an inference engine: it exposes one OpenAI- (or native-)format API across 100+ upstream providers, including vLLM, NVIDIA NIM and self-hosted OpenAI-compatible servers.
Rust core with a Python SDK, positioned by the project as a fast, lightweight gateway.
Cost tracking, guardrails, load balancing and logging as first-class features.
Native provider formats, not just OpenAI-shaped: Anthropic, Bedrock and Vertex requests pass through with their own shapes where needed.
Helm chart, Terraform and vscode-extension in-repo for deployment.
hardware_caveats: This record has no local compute backend and that is the point: LiteLLM never loads weights and never touches a GPU, CPU or NPU. supported_backends is recorded as an explicit 'none' rather than left empty so a reader querying by backend does not mistake it for a missing value.
Latency is added, not removed. Every request pays at least one extra network hop, so it is the wrong layer for a single-user local model — it exists for fleets.
Licensing is split: everything outside the enterprise/ directory is MIT, everything under it is under enterprise/LICENSE. Embedding in a product needs the license split read, not just the repo badge.
Because it routes across providers, an upstream that lacks a feature makes that feature appear intermittently missing — the gateway unifies the API surface, not the capability surface.
best_for: One API key and one billing surface across many cloud providers.
Fallback and load balancing across heterogeneous deployments — including a local llama.cpp or vLLM box as one target among cloud providers.
Cost attribution and observability for LLM traffic, with an OpenTelemetry flush endpoint.
Teams standardizing on the OpenAI shape so a model or vendor can be swapped without touching application code.
MCP gatewaying in front of many tools or models.
avoid_for: Single-user local inference — pure added latency and an extra process.
Anything where you need the model's throughput characteristics to be what you measure end to end.
Cutting dependency count; a Rust core plus Python SDK plus provider SDKs is not minimal.
Any assumption that API compatibility implies capability parity across providers.
notes: Included per the delegated brief's allowance for a genuinely distinct serving/routing layer. It is deliberately scoped to the routing/proxy role and touches no inference kernel, so it does not overlap the GPU-serving engines other agents cover. supported_formats records passthrough behaviour rather than weight formats because no weight format reaches this layer — a weight-format query against this record will correctly return nothing useful.
